GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2019-07-31T19:55:52Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Crypto: Is it safe to pool X509Chain objects without resetting the X509ChainPolicy?
Description: I’m building a high-throughput message broker in .net core (2.1 today, upgrading to 3.0-preview7 soon), and need to do client certificate based authentication with a custom cert chain (that I set up on the chain.ChainPolicy.ExtraStore).

To reduce GC pressure, I tend to pool all the byte arrays / batch message arrays / etc.

Is it a good idea to also pool X509Chain objects? And not do a chain.Policy.Reset call on every rent/return?

It’s the X509ChainPolicy.ExtraStore allocation and 5x X509ChainPolicy.ExtraStore.Add(customCert) calls that lead to array resizing, that I want to avoid.

-	When the chain is returned to the pool, I dispose off all the chainElement.Certificate objects and do a chain.Reset() to dispose off the _pal object.
-	I am explicitly resetting chain.ChainPolicy.VerificationTime to DateTime.Now after every pool.Rent().

In other words - Does the X509ChainPolicy ever end up holding on to any valid / invalid state from an old call to chain.Build()?

I couldn’t find anything in the source code that says the Policy leads to any cross-talk between multiple chain.Build() calls using the same Policy object, but still wanted someone from corefx to weigh in and give an all clear.

Thanks!

cc @bartonjs @stephentoub
